title: Model Immunization from a Condition Number Perspective
reviewed_version: PMLR 267 published version fetched from supplied mlresearch source URL
summary: Two exact counterexamples invalidate core theoretical derivations; one local transpose inconsistency in released preconditioning.
limitations: No author code or training executed.
No historical implementation identity or empirical effect inferred.
Rank-changing ill-regularizer domain and complete Theorem 4.3(2) not certified.
Later revisions and author adoption unknown.
Test-accuracy early stopping merits clarification; bias magnitude unestablished.

problems.claim: Proposition 3.2 Eq.(10) lists singular values of theta^T K theta
problems.result: eigenvalues 5 +/- sqrt(13), whereas charitable formula gives 8,2 and literal gamma convention gives 20,5
problems.counterevidence: Aligned eigenbases are a valid special case; both gamma interpretations tested; PDF equations visually confirmed
problems.impact: Invalid core spectral derivation in section 3.1; does not negate experiments
problems.correction: Spectrum is eigenvalues of Sigma U^T K U Sigma, not its diagonal

problems.claim: Theorem 4.3(1) guarantees decreasing condition number for displayed step interval
problems.counterevidence: Both matrices stay full rank and theta stays positive diagonal; isolated regularizer; smaller steps may succeed
problems.impact: False central monotonic-decrease guarantee; no claim about historical learning-rate outcomes

problems.check: Compare left and right multiplication by diag(3,2)^(-1)

P1.source: Re-read physical PDF pp.3,13-14: Eq.(10) and Appendix B.1 use only the SVD and PSD Gram assumption, without alignment.
P1.independent_argument: For theta=diag(2,1) and K=[[2,1],[1,2]], det(tI-theta^T K theta)=t^2-10t+12, hence 5 +/- sqrt(13); the claimed diagonal list is [8,2] under Gamma^2 and [20,5] under literal gamma. K eigenvalues 3,1 ensure a real invertible X=K^(1/2); theta is square/full rank. Normalized M rows have dot product 1/2, so the assertion O^T O=I fails.
P1.alternative_and_dependency: Alignment makes the row correlations vanish, but is not assumed. The factor-two least-squares Hessian convention cannot rescue either spectrum. This invalidates the central Section 3.1 spectral derivation, not empirical efficacy.
P1.severity_and_repair: Major retained. Orthogonal similarity to Sigma U^T K U Sigma is a proved replacement identity, not a certification of all angle-based claims.

P2.source: Read pp.4-5 Theorem 4.3 and p.22 ordering argument; viewed original p.4 to distinguish the 2/d^2 denominator.
P2.independent_argument: d=2, K=I, theta=diag(2,1), H=diag(4,1), eta=1/5 meet uniqueness, invertibility and 0<eta<min(1/2,2). Differentiating Rwell=||H||_2^2/2-||H||_F^2/4 via dH gives gradient diag(8,-1), hence Hnew=diag(4/25,36/25) and kappa=9 instead of 4. The old leading mode becomes the smaller one.
P2.alternative_and_dependency: No full-loss interaction, zero-rank convention or sign reversal of theta is involved. Section 4.4 combined-loss limitation therefore does not address this failure of the separate guarantee.
P2.severity_and_repair: Major retained for the core regularizer guarantee. Directly solving 1/2 < 2(1-4eta)/(1+eta) < 2 verifies the reported sufficient example interval (0,3/17); it is not a universal repair or a claim of the complete success set.

references.anchors: claim that sigma P,1 prime remains maximal

P3.source: Read Figure 4/p.26, released linear.py forward/backward and model.py reg_loss enablement.
P3.independent_argument: Because Y=XW^T=Xtheta, gradient transforms as Gtheta=GW^T; transpose of K_lambda^-1 Gtheta is GW K_lambda^-1. The release instead solves K_lambda GW. With K_lambda=diag(3,2) and off-diagonal GW, two outputs differ by [[0,-1/6],[1/6,0]], norm sqrt(2)/6. An invertible input permits the chosen upstream gradient.
P3.alternative_and_dependency: Commuting gradients agree; ridge also changes exact inverse but does not resolve axis mismatch. Current static code identity is established, historical execution and measured influence are not.
P3.severity_and_repair: Minor retained. Right multiplication/transposed solve restores the local convention only; no full training repair is claimed.
